subject: maths
title: Primary 6 Dividing Fractions
seo_title: P6 Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE Practice)
standard_text: Dividing a proper fraction by a whole number, and a whole number or proper fraction by a proper fraction, without calculator
meta_desc: Free P6 maths practice on dividing fractions for the PSLE: fraction ÷ whole number, whole number ÷ fraction, fraction ÷ fraction. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: To divide by a fraction or a whole number, multiply by its reciprocal. Flip only the divisor.
body_html:
The big idea

Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. The reciprocal of 34 is 43, and the reciprocal of 5 is 15. Flip only the divisor, the number after ÷. Then simplify.

Fraction ÷ whole number

Dividing by 4 means sharing into 4 equal parts. It is the same as multiplying by 14.

Example 1

23 ÷ 4 = ?

23 ÷ 4 = 23 × 14 = 212. Simplify by dividing the numerator and the denominator by 2.

Answer: 16

Whole number ÷ fraction

3 ÷ 14 asks: how many quarters are there in 3?

Example 2

6 ÷ 34 = ?

Multiply by the reciprocal of 34: 6 × 43 = 243 = 8. Check: 8 × 34 = 244 = 6.

Answer: 8

Fraction ÷ fraction

Ask how many groups of the divisor fit, or multiply by the reciprocal.

Example 3

34 ÷ 38 = ?

34 × 83. The 3s cancel, and 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so the answer is 2. Check: 2 × 38 = 68 = 34.

Answer: 2

Example 4

12 ÷ 34 = ?

12 × 43 = 46 = 23. The answer is less than 1, because 34 does not fit into 12 even once.

Answer: 23

Word problems: units and parts

Draw a bar model. Find the value of 1 unit first.

Example 5

23 of a bottle holds 12 ℓ of water. How much does the full bottle hold?

2 units = 12 ℓ. 1 unit = 12 ÷ 2 = 14 ℓ. 3 units = 3 × 14 = 34 ℓ. In one step: 12 ÷ 23 = 12 × 32 = 34.

Answer: 34 ℓ

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
23 ÷ 45 = 32 × 45 (flipping the first fraction)Flip only the divisor: 23 × 54 = 56
37 ÷ 34 = 37 × 34 (not flipping)Use the reciprocal: 37 × 43 = 47
25 ÷ 4 = 85 (multiplying the numerator by 4)Multiply the denominator: 220 = 110
6 ÷ 34 = 2 (dividing by the numerator only)6 × 43 = 8
58 ÷ 56 = 3040 (not in simplest form)Simplify: 3040 = 34

faq.q: How do you divide fractions in Primary 6?
faq.a: Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor, then simplify. For example, 3/4 ÷ 3/8 = 3/4 × 8/3 = 2, and 2/3 ÷ 4 = 2/3 × 1/4 = 1/6.

faq.q: How do I explain dividing by a fraction to my child?
faq.a: Ask “how many of these fit?”. 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many quarters there are in 3, and a bar cut into quarters shows there are 12.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when dividing fractions?
faq.a: Flipping the wrong fraction. Only the divisor (the number after ÷) is flipped, so 2/3 ÷ 4/5 = 2/3 × 5/4 = 5/6, not 3/2 × 4/5.

faq.q: Is dividing fractions tested in the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. Dividing a proper fraction by a whole number or by a proper fraction is in the MOE Primary 6 syllabus, and the PSLE tests it in calculations without a calculator and in word problems.

sets.title: Divide a fraction by a whole number

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 13. It is divided into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
13 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the lines across the bar: the whole is cut into 3 × 2 = 6 equal parts, and 1 of them is dark: 16. Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12: 13 ÷ 2 = 13 × 12 = 16. Check: 16 × 2 = 26 = 13.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 12. It is divided into 4 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
12 ÷ 4 = ?
items.e: Follow the lines across the bar: the whole is cut into 2 × 4 = 8 equal parts, and 1 of them is dark: 18. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14: 12 ÷ 4 = 12 × 14 = 18. Check: 18 × 4 = 48 = 12.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 23. It is divided into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
23 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the lines across the bar: the whole is cut into 3 × 2 = 6 equal parts, and 2 of them are dark: 26 = 13. The numerator 2 can be divided by 2: 2 ÷ 2 = 1. Keep the denominator: 23 ÷ 2 = 13. Check: 13 × 2 = 23.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 34. It is divided into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
34 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the lines across the bar: the whole is cut into 4 × 2 = 8 equal parts, and 3 of them are dark: 38. Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12: 34 ÷ 2 = 34 × 12 = 38. Check: 38 × 2 = 68 = 34.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 25. It is divided into 3 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
25 ÷ 3 = ?
items.e: Follow the lines across the bar: the whole is cut into 5 × 3 = 15 equal parts, and 2 of them are dark: 215. Dividing by 3 is the same as multiplying by 13: 25 ÷ 3 = 25 × 13 = 215. Check: 215 × 3 = 615 = 25.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 45. It is divided into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
45 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the lines across the bar: the whole is cut into 5 × 2 = 10 equal parts, and 4 of them are dark: 410 = 25. The numerator 4 can be divided by 2: 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Keep the denominator: 45 ÷ 2 = 25. Check: 25 × 2 = 45.

items.q: 15 ÷ 4 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14: 15 ÷ 4 = 15 × 14 = 120. Check: 120 × 4 = 420 = 15.

items.q:
47 ÷ 2 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The numerator 4 can be divided by 2: 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Keep the denominator: 47 ÷ 2 = 27. Check: 27 × 2 = 47.

items.q:
611 ÷ 3 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The numerator 6 can be divided by 3: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Keep the denominator: 611 ÷ 3 = 211. Check: 211 × 3 = 611.

items.q: 38 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12: 38 ÷ 2 = 38 × 12 = 316. Check: 316 × 2 = 616 = 38.

items.q:
29 ÷ 4 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14: 29 ÷ 4 = 29 × 14 = 236. Simplify: 236 = 118. Check: 118 × 4 = 418 = 29.

items.q:
35 ÷ 6 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 6 is the same as multiplying by 16: 35 ÷ 6 = 35 × 16 = 330. Simplify: 330 = 110. Check: 110 × 6 = 610 = 35.

items.q:
56 ÷ 10 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 10 is the same as multiplying by 110: 56 ÷ 10 = 56 × 110 = 560. Simplify: 560 = 112. Check: 112 × 10 = 1012 = 56.

items.q:
89 ÷ 4 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The numerator 8 can be divided by 4: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Keep the denominator: 89 ÷ 4 = 29. Check: 29 × 4 = 89.

items.q: 310 ÷ 4 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14: 310 ÷ 4 = 310 × 14 = 340. Check: 340 × 4 = 1240 = 310.

items.q:
49 ÷ 6 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 6 is the same as multiplying by 16: 49 ÷ 6 = 49 × 16 = 454. Simplify: 454 = 227. Check: 227 × 6 = 1227 = 49.

items.q: Dividing by 5 is the same as …
items.e: Sharing into 5 equal parts gives 15 of the amount each, so dividing by 5 is the same as multiplying by 15. 5 and 15 are reciprocals: 5 × 15 = 1.

items.q: Which multiplication has the same answer as 34 ÷ 6?
c: 34 × 16
43 × 16
items.e: Keep 34 and multiply by the reciprocal of 6, which is 16: 34 × 16 = 324 = 18. Do not flip 34.

items.q: Hui Min says 25 ÷ 4 = 85. What mistake did she make?
c: She multiplied by 4 instead of dividing.
She flipped 25 instead of using the reciprocal of 4.
She multiplied the numerator and the denominator by 4.
items.e: Hui Min worked out 25 × 4 = 85. Dividing a fraction by a whole number makes it smaller. 25 ÷ 4 = 25 × 14 = 220 = 110. So she multiplied by 4 instead of dividing.

items.q: Zhi Hao says 45 ÷ 2 = 58. What mistake did he make?
c: He multiplied the numerator and the denominator by 2.
He flipped 45 instead of using the reciprocal of 2.
He multiplied by 2 instead of dividing.
items.e: Zhi Hao worked out 54 × 12 = 58. Only the divisor is flipped: 45 ÷ 2 = 45 × 12 = 410 = 25. So he flipped 45 instead of using the reciprocal of 2.

sets.title: Divide a whole number by a fraction

items.q:
The bar shows 3 wholes, each cut into quarters. How many quarters are there in 3?
3 ÷ 14 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 4 quarters, so 3 wholes have 3 × 4 = 12 quarters. So 3 ÷ 14 = 12. Check: 12 × 14 = 3.

items.q:
The bar shows 2 wholes, each cut into thirds. How many thirds are there in 2?
2 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 3 thirds, so 2 wholes have 2 × 3 = 6 thirds. So 2 ÷ 13 = 6. Check: 6 × 13 = 2.

items.q:
The bar shows 4 wholes, each cut into halves. How many halves are there in 4?
4 ÷ 12 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 2 halves, so 4 wholes have 4 × 2 = 8 halves. So 4 ÷ 12 = 8. Check: 8 × 12 = 4.

items.q:
The bar shows 2 wholes, each cut into fifths. How many fifths are there in 2?
2 ÷ 15 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 5 fifths, so 2 wholes have 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. So 2 ÷ 15 = 10. Check: 10 × 15 = 2.

items.q:
The bar shows 3 wholes, each cut into sixths. How many sixths are there in 3?
3 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 6 sixths, so 3 wholes have 3 × 6 = 18 sixths. So 3 ÷ 16 = 18. Check: 18 × 16 = 3.

items.q:
The bar shows 5 wholes, each cut into thirds. How many thirds are there in 5?
5 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 3 thirds, so 5 wholes have 5 × 3 = 15 thirds. So 5 ÷ 13 = 15. Check: 15 × 13 = 5.

items.q:
How many groups of 23 are there in 2?
2 ÷ 23 = ?
items.e: Count in thirds: 2 = 63. Each group is 2 thirds. 6 thirds make 6 ÷ 2 = 3 groups. So 2 ÷ 23 = 3. Check: 3 × 23 = 2.

items.q:
How many groups of 34 are there in 3?
3 ÷ 34 = ?
items.e: Count in quarters: 3 = 124. Each group is 3 quarters. 12 quarters make 12 ÷ 3 = 4 groups. So 3 ÷ 34 = 4. Check: 4 × 34 = 3.

items.q:
How many groups of 25 are there in 4?
4 ÷ 25 = ?
items.e: Count in fifths: 4 = 205. Each group is 2 fifths. 20 fifths make 20 ÷ 2 = 10 groups. So 4 ÷ 25 = 10. Check: 10 × 25 = 4.

items.q:
How many groups of 45 are there in 2?
2 ÷ 45 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Count in fifths: 2 = 105. Each group is 4 fifths. 10 fifths make 2 full groups, with 2 fifths left over. Those 2 fifths are 24 of a group. So 2 ÷ 45 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 × 45 = 2.

items.q:
How many groups of 23 are there in 3?
3 ÷ 23 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Count in thirds: 3 = 93. Each group is 2 thirds. 9 thirds make 4 full groups, with 1 third left over. That 1 third is 12 of a group. So 3 ÷ 23 = 4 12. Check: 4 12 × 23 = 3.

items.q: 6 ÷ 34 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 43: 6 ÷ 34 = 6 × 43. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 3 by 3. Now 2 × 4 = 8. Check: 8 × 34 = 6.

items.q: 8 ÷ 23 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 23 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 32: 8 ÷ 23 = 8 × 32. Cancel common factors first: divide 8 and 2 by 2. Now 4 × 3 = 12. Check: 12 × 23 = 8.

items.q:
4 ÷ 35 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 35 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 53: 4 ÷ 35 = 4 × 53 = 4 × 51 × 3 = 203 = 6 23. Check: 6 23 × 35 = 4.

items.q: 9 ÷ 37 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 37 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 73: 9 ÷ 37 = 9 × 73. Cancel common factors first: divide 9 and 3 by 3. Now 3 × 7 = 21. Check: 21 × 37 = 9.

items.q: 5 ÷ 56 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 56 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 65: 5 ÷ 56 = 5 × 65. Cancel common factors first: the 5s cancel. Now 1 × 6 = 6. Check: 6 × 56 = 5.

items.q:
7 ÷ 23 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 23 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 32: 7 ÷ 23 = 7 × 32 = 7 × 31 × 2 = 212 = 10 12. Check: 10 12 × 23 = 7.

items.q: 10 ÷ 58 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 58 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 85: 10 ÷ 58 = 10 × 85. Cancel common factors first: divide 10 and 5 by 5. Now 2 × 8 = 16. Check: 16 × 58 = 10.

items.q: How many fifths are there in 4?
items.e: Each whole has 5 fifths, so 4 wholes have 4 × 5 = 20 fifths. This is 4 ÷ 15 = 4 × 5 = 20.

items.q: How many groups of 23 are there in 6?
items.e: 6 ÷ 23 = 6 × 32 = 182 = 9. Check: 9 × 23 = 183 = 6.

sets.title: Divide a fraction by a fraction

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 35?
items.e: Swap the numerator and the denominator: the reciprocal of 35 is 53. Check: 35 × 53 = 1515 = 1.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 17?
items.e: Swap the numerator and the denominator: 17 becomes 71 = 7. Check: 17 × 7 = 1.

items.q: Which multiplication has the same answer as 23 ÷ 57?
c: 23 × 75
32 × 57
23 × 57
32 × 75
items.e: Keep the first fraction and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor 57, which is 75: 23 × 75. Do not flip 23.

items.q: Which multiplication has the same answer as 49 ÷ 16?
c: 94 × 16
49 × 16
items.e: Keep the first fraction and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor 16, which is 6: 49 × 6. Do not flip 49.

items.q:
The bar shows 23. How many groups of 16 are there in 23?
23 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: Count in sixths: 23 = 46. Each group is 1 sixth. 4 sixths make 4 ÷ 1 = 4 groups. So 23 ÷ 16 = 4. Check: 4 × 16 = 23.

items.q:
The bar shows 34. How many groups of 38 are there in 34?
34 ÷ 38 = ?
items.e: Count in eighths: 34 = 68. Each group is 3 eighths. 6 eighths make 6 ÷ 3 = 2 groups. So 34 ÷ 38 = 2. Check: 2 × 38 = 34.

items.q:
The bar shows 56. How many groups of 13 are there in 56?
56 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Count in sixths: 13 = 26. Each group is 2 sixths. 5 sixths make 2 full groups, with 1 sixth left over. That 1 sixth is 12 of a group. So 56 ÷ 13 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 × 13 = 56.

items.q:
12 ÷ 34 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 43: 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43. Cancel common factors first: divide 4 and 2 by 2. Now 1 × 23 = 23. Check: 23 × 34 = 12.

items.q:
25 ÷ 45 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 45 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 54: 25 ÷ 45 = 25 × 54. Cancel common factors first: divide 2 and 4 by 2, and the 5s cancel. Now 1 × 12 = 12. Check: 12 × 45 = 25.

items.q:
67 ÷ 27 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 27 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 72: 67 ÷ 27 = 67 × 72. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 2 by 2, and the 7s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3. Check: 3 × 27 = 67.

items.q:
38 ÷ 14 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 14 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 4: 38 ÷ 14 = 38 × 4. Cancel common factors first: divide 4 and 8 by 4. Now 32 × 1 = 32 = 1 12. Check: 1 12 × 14 = 38.

items.q:
59 ÷ 23 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 23 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 32: 59 ÷ 23 = 59 × 32. Cancel common factors first: divide 3 and 9 by 3. Now 53 × 12 = 56. Check: 56 × 23 = 59.

items.q:
710 ÷ 35 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 35 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 53: 710 ÷ 35 = 710 × 53. Cancel common factors first: divide 5 and 10 by 5. Now 72 × 13 = 76 = 1 16. Check: 1 16 × 35 = 710.

items.q:
58 ÷ 56 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 56 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 65: 58 ÷ 56 = 58 × 65. Cancel common factors first: the 5s cancel, and divide 6 and 8 by 2. Now 14 × 3 = 34. Check: 34 × 56 = 58.

items.q:
310 ÷ 920 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 920 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 209: 310 ÷ 920 = 310 × 209. Cancel common factors first: divide 3 and 9 by 3, and divide 20 and 10 by 10. Now 1 × 23 = 23. Check: 23 × 920 = 310.

items.q:
16 ÷ 49 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 49 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 94: 16 ÷ 49 = 16 × 94. Cancel common factors first: divide 9 and 6 by 3. Now 12 × 34 = 38. Check: 38 × 49 = 16.

items.q:
89 ÷ 23 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 23 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 32: 89 ÷ 23 = 89 × 32. Cancel common factors first: divide 8 and 2 by 2, and divide 3 and 9 by 3. Now 43 × 1 = 43 = 1 13. Check: 1 13 × 23 = 89.

items.q:
34 ÷ 56 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 56 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 65: 34 ÷ 56 = 34 × 65. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 4 by 2. Now 32 × 35 = 910. Check: 910 × 56 = 34.

items.q:
910 ÷ 34 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 43: 910 ÷ 34 = 910 × 43. Cancel common factors first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and divide 4 and 10 by 2. Now 35 × 2 = 65 = 1 15. Check: 1 15 × 34 = 910.

items.q:
1112 ÷ 23 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 23 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 32: 1112 ÷ 23 = 1112 × 32. Cancel common factors first: divide 3 and 12 by 3. Now 114 × 12 = 118 = 1 38. Check: 1 38 × 23 = 1112.

sets.title: Mixed practice and checking by multiplying

items.q:
56 ÷ 5 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The numerator 5 can be divided by 5: 5 ÷ 5 = 1. Keep the denominator: 56 ÷ 5 = 16. Check: 16 × 5 = 56.

items.q:
4 ÷ 27 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 27 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 72: 4 ÷ 27 = 4 × 72. Cancel common factors first: divide 4 and 2 by 2. Now 2 × 7 = 14. Check: 14 × 27 = 4.

items.q:
35 ÷ 910 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 910 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 109: 35 ÷ 910 = 35 × 109. Cancel common factors first: divide 3 and 9 by 3, and divide 10 and 5 by 5. Now 1 × 23 = 23. Check: 23 × 910 = 35.

items.q:
910 ÷ 6 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 6 is the same as multiplying by 16: 910 ÷ 6 = 910 × 16 = 960. Simplify: 960 = 320. Check: 320 × 6 = 1820 = 910.

items.q:
12 ÷ 34 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 43: 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43. Cancel common factors first: divide 12 and 3 by 3. Now 4 × 4 = 16. Check: 16 × 34 = 12.

items.q:
29 ÷ 56 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 56 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 65: 29 ÷ 56 = 29 × 65. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 9 by 3. Now 23 × 25 = 415. Check: 415 × 56 = 29.

items.q:
611 ÷ 322 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 322 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 223: 611 ÷ 322 = 611 × 223. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 3 by 3, and divide 22 and 11 by 11. Now 2 × 2 = 4. Check: 4 × 322 = 611.

items.q:
3 ÷ 49 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 49 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 94: 3 ÷ 49 = 3 × 94 = 3 × 91 × 4 = 274 = 6 34. Check: 6 34 × 49 = 3.

items.q:
512 ÷ 10 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Dividing by 10 is the same as multiplying by 110: 512 ÷ 10 = 512 × 110 = 5120. Simplify: 5120 = 124. Check: 124 × 10 = 1024 = 512.

items.q: Which multiplication checks that 34 ÷ 38 = 2?
c: 34 × 38
items.e: Answer × divisor should give the number you started with: 2 × 38 = 68 = 34.

items.q: Wei Ming works out 56 ÷ 23 = 1 14. Which calculation checks his answer?
c: 1 14 × 56
1 14 ÷ 23
1 14 × 23
56 × 23
items.e: Multiply the answer by the divisor: 1 14 × 23 = 54 × 23 = 1012 = 56. This is 56, so his answer is correct.

items.q: Which multiplication checks that 8 ÷ 23 = 12?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the divisor: 12 × 23 = 243 = 8.

items.q: Farah says 34 ÷ 25 = 1 78. Is she correct?
c: No, the answer should be 815
Yes, because 1 78 × 25 = 34
No, the answer should be 310
No, because 1 78 × 25 = 38
items.e: Check by multiplying: 1 78 × 25 = 158 × 25 = 3040 = 34. This is the number she started with, so yes, because 1 78 × 25 = 34.

items.q: Ryan says 49 ÷ 23 = 827. He checks by multiplying. What does he find?
c: 827 × 23 is not 49, so the answer is 32
827 × 23 is not 49, so the answer is 23
827 × 23 = 49, so he is correct
827 × 23 is not 49, so the answer is 94
items.e: 827 × 23 = 1681, which is not 49, so he made a mistake: he multiplied instead of dividing. 49 ÷ 23 = 49 × 32 = 1218 = 23. So 827 × 23 is not 49, so the answer is 23.

items.q: ? ÷ 14 = 12
items.e: Undo the division by multiplying: ? = 12 × 14 = 124 = 3. Check: 3 ÷ 14 = 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: 56 ÷ ? = 2 12
items.e: The divisor = 56 ÷ 2 12 = 56 ÷ 52 = 56 × 25 = 1030 = 13. Check: 56 ÷ 13 = 56 × 3 = 156 = 2 12.

items.q: Kavya writes 23 ÷ 45 = 32 × 45 = 65. What mistake did she make?
c: She flipped the first fraction instead of the divisor.
She did not flip either fraction.
items.e: Only the divisor 45 is flipped: 23 × 54 = 1012 = 56. So she flipped the first fraction instead of the divisor.

items.q: Arjun writes 37 ÷ 34 = 37 × 34 = 928. What mistake did he make?
c: He did not use the reciprocal of 34.
items.e: He multiplied by 34 itself. Multiply by its reciprocal 43: 37 × 43 = 47. The 3s cancel. So he did not use the reciprocal of 34.

items.q: Sarah works out 58 ÷ 56 and gets 3040. What should she do next?
c: Flip it to 4030.
Nothing. 3040 is the final answer.
Simplify it to 310.
Simplify it to 34.
items.e: 3040 is correct in value but not in its simplest form. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 10: simplify it to 34.

items.q: Which division has an answer greater than 1?
c: 34 ÷ 12
12 ÷ 34
25 ÷ 45
items.e: When the number you divide is greater than the divisor, the answer is greater than 1. 34 is greater than 12, and 34 ÷ 12 = 34 × 2 = 64 = 1 12.

items.q: Nurul has a ribbon 34 m long. She cuts it into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3 units = 34 m. 1 unit = 34 ÷ 3. The numerator 3 can be divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1. Keep the denominator: 34 ÷ 3 = 14 m. Check: 14 × 3 = 34.

items.q: Ethan has 23 of a cake. He shares it equally among himself and 3 friends. What fraction of the whole cake does each person get?
c: 14 of the cake
27 of the cake
29 of the cake
16 of the cake
items.e: Ethan and 3 friends make 4 people, so divide by 4, not 3. 4 units = 23. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14: 23 ÷ 4 = 23 × 14 = 212. Simplify: 212 = 16 of the cake. Check: 16 × 4 = 46 = 23.

items.q: Mdm Wong has 6 ℓ of soya bean milk. She pours all of it into bottles. Each bottle holds 34 ℓ. How many bottles does she fill?
items.e: How many 34 ℓ are there in 6 ℓ? Dividing by 34 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 43: 6 ÷ 34 = 6 × 43. Cancel common factors first: divide 6 and 3 by 3. Now 2 × 4 = 8 bottles. Check: 8 × 34 = 6.

items.q: Siti has 34 kg of sugar. She uses 18 kg of sugar for each tray of kueh. How many trays of kueh can she make?
items.e: How many 18 kg are there in 34 kg? Dividing by 18 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 8: 34 ÷ 18 = 34 × 8. Cancel common factors first: divide 8 and 4 by 4. Now 3 × 2 = 6 trays. Check: 6 × 18 = 34.

items.q: Devi has 5 ℓ of syrup. She pours it into bottles that each hold 58 ℓ. Which expression gives the number of bottles she fills?
items.e: The question asks how many 58 ℓ there are in 5 ℓ, so divide: 5 ÷ 58 = 5 × 85 = 8 bottles.

items.q: Hafiz pours 34 ℓ of water equally into some cups. Each cup has 320 ℓ of water. How many cups are there?
items.e: How many 320 ℓ are there in 34 ℓ? Dividing by 320 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 203: 34 ÷ 320 = 34 × 203. Cancel common factors first: the 3s cancel, and divide 20 and 4 by 4. Now 1 × 5 = 5 cups. Check: 5 × 320 = 34.

items.q: One round of a cycling path at East Coast Park is 25 km. Ryan cycles 4 km. How many rounds does he cycle?
items.e: How many 25 km are there in 4 km? Dividing by 25 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 52: 4 ÷ 25 = 4 × 52. Cancel common factors first: divide 4 and 2 by 2. Now 2 × 5 = 10 rounds. Check: 10 × 25 = 4.

items.q: Mrs Ng buys 5 ℓ of orange juice for a Children’s Day party. Each student gets 18 ℓ. How many students get a cup of juice?
items.e: How many 18 ℓ are there in 5 ℓ? Dividing by 18 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 8: 5 ÷ 18 = 5 × 8 = 40 students. Check: 40 × 18 = 5.

items.q: 23 of a bottle holds 12 ℓ of water. How much water does the full bottle hold?
items.e: 2 units = 12 ℓ, so 1 unit = 14 ℓ and 3 units = 34 ℓ. Or divide in one step. Dividing by 23 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 32: 12 ÷ 23 = 12 × 32 = 1 × 32 × 2 = 34 ℓ. Check: 34 × 23 = 12.

items.q: Mr Rahman uses 34 of a tin of paint to paint 6 identical shelves. What fraction of a tin of paint does he use for each shelf?
c: 29 of a tin
4 12 of a tin
310 of a tin
18 of a tin
items.e: Share 34 among 6 shelves. Dividing by 6 is the same as multiplying by 16: 34 ÷ 6 = 34 × 16 = 324. Simplify: 324 = 18 of a tin. Check: 18 × 6 = 68 = 34.

items.q: A rectangular garden plot at a void deck has an area of 23 m². Its width is 45 m. What is its length?
items.e: Length = area ÷ width. Dividing by 45 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 54: 23 ÷ 45 = 23 × 54. Cancel common factors first: divide 2 and 4 by 2. Now 13 × 52 = 56 m. Check: 56 × 45 = 23.

items.q: Raju has 4 m of rope. He cuts as many pieces as he can, each 35 m long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: 4 ÷ 35 = 4 × 53 = 203 = 6 23. Only full pieces count, so he gets 6 pieces. Check: 6 × 35 = 185 = 3 35 m, which is less than 4 m, but 7 pieces would need 4 15 m.

items.q: Kumar has 3 m of wire. He cuts as many pieces as he can, each 25 m long. What length of wire is left over?
items.e: 3 ÷ 25 = 3 × 52 = 152 = 7 12, so he cuts 7 full pieces. 7 × 25 = 145 = 2 45 m. Left over: 3 − 2 45 = 15 m. (The 12 is half of a piece, not 12 m.)

items.q: Mrs Lim has 45 kg of beef. She cooks 14 of it. She divides the rest equally into 3 packets. What is the mass of the beef in each packet?
items.e: Cut the bar into 4 units: she cooks 1 unit and 3 units are left. 4 units = 45 kg, so 1 unit = 45 ÷ 4 = 15 kg. Each packet holds 1 unit: 15 kg. (415 kg is the whole 45 kg ÷ 3, but she cooked some first.)

items.q: Sarah buys 34 kg of grapes. She eats 16 kg and shares the rest equally among 7 friends. What mass of grapes does each friend get?
items.e: The rest: 34 − 16 = 912 − 212 = 712 kg. Share it among 7: 712 ÷ 7 = 112 kg. Check: 7 × 112 = 712 kg.

items.q: Priya has a ribbon 2 m long. She uses 13 of it to wrap a present. She cuts the rest into pieces, each 29 m long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: She uses 13 of 2 m = 23 m. The rest is 2 − 23 = 1 13 m = 43 m. 43 ÷ 29 = 43 × 92 = 366 = 6 pieces. (9 pieces would use the whole 2 m, and 3 pieces is the part she used.)

items.q: Jar A has 34 ℓ of honey and Jar B has 12 ℓ of honey. All the honey is poured into small bottles of 18 ℓ each. How many bottles are filled?
items.e: Total honey: 34 + 12 = 34 + 24 = 54 ℓ. 54 ÷ 18 = 54 × 8 = 10 bottles. (6 bottles is for Jar A only. Do not add the fractions as 46.)

items.q: A hawker uses 35 kg of noodles to cook 4 plates of fried noodles. Each plate has the same mass of noodles. How many plates can she cook with 3 kg of noodles?
items.e: Each plate: 35 ÷ 4 = 320 kg. Number of plates: 3 ÷ 320 = 3 × 203 = 603 = 20 plates. (5 is the number of times 35 kg goes into 3 kg; each of those makes 4 plates: 5 × 4 = 20.)

items.q: Ali uses 25 of a tin of paint to paint 3 identical chairs. How many such chairs can he paint with 2 tins of paint?
items.e: Each chair: 25 ÷ 3 = 215 of a tin. Number of chairs: 2 ÷ 215 = 2 × 152 = 302 = 15 chairs. Check: 15 × 215 = 3015 = 2 tins.

items.q: Mei Ling cuts a ribbon 34 m long into 3 equal pieces. Jun Jie cuts a ribbon 23 m long into 2 equal pieces. How much longer is each of Jun Jie’s pieces than each of Mei Ling’s pieces?
items.e: Mei Ling: 34 ÷ 3 = 14 m. Jun Jie: 23 ÷ 2 = 13 m. Difference: 13 − 14 = 412 − 312 = 112 m.
